goal: Speed up initial sync of block filter index and tx index by processing blocks in parallel instead of one at a time
Lets users enable these indexes on an already-synced node without waiting many hours
reviewability: Paused: author is holding this PR until the standalone ThreadPool work in #33689 lands, then will rebase
Marked needs_rebase and draft, and conflicts with other open PRs including the author's own follow-up
agreement: Disputed: concept and approach ACKs exist but a later Approach NACK raises unresolved concerns
Approach NACK backed by cross-platform benchmarks showing txindex parallel sync is slower not faster (l0rinc)
Independently confirmed txindex slowdown on a 32-vCPU machine (andrewtoth)
Approach ACK after a deep review pass calling the design nice and reasonable (ryanofsky)
Code review ACK and re-ACK after building and running a mainnet sync comparison (pinheadmz)
Author countered with own benchmarks showing speedups but has not resolved the discrepancy

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because it targets initial sync time, a multi-hour pain point users of these indexes feel directly
Testers measured large blockfilterindex speedups on SSD, but txindex parallel sync can be slower than sequential for others
Also lays groundwork for a follow-up PR that batches DB writes, benefiting sequential syncs too

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because the new fuzz harness caught a real timeout-adjacent bug in the ThreadPool's stop logic
Coverage exists mainly to support this PR's new utility rather than a widely-used high-risk path

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because a correct reusable ThreadPool reduces duplicated threading work across multiple future efforts
Already being adopted for the HTTP worker queue and a validation input-fetcher effort elsewhere
Extensive review of memory-ordering and shutdown-safety shows this is a primitive where subtle bugs matter node-wide
